speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) whether any individuals sanctioned by the US for alleged transnational criminal activities or convicted in Singapore's largest money laundering case had operated tax-exempt family offices locally; (b) what due diligence checks does MAS conduct before granting such incentives; and (c) what systemic reforms have been implemented to prevent criminal networks from exploiting Singapore's family office regime.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Singapore upholds high regulatory standards in our financial system aligned with international standards.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: It is one reason why many investors view Singapore as a trusted financial hub.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Like other global financial centres, having high standards does not mean there will be zero cases involving entities and individuals who break the rules or who fail to comply with our regulatory requirements.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: What is key is that where wrongdoing is identified, the authorities will investigate thoroughly and take firm enforcement action in accordance with the law.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The money laundering investigations by the Police against Chen Zhi and related associates are ongoing.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Enforcement operations were conducted on 30 October 2025.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Arising from the enforcement operations, the Police have issued prohibition of disposal orders and seized a range of assets, including properties, cars, bank accounts and securities accounts.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: As investigations are ongoing, I seek Members’ understanding that I am not able to comment further on the details at this stage.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Besides the rejected applications, some potential applicants also withdrew their interest to apply before submitting a formal application when questions were posed and requirements were clarified at the pre-application stage.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: As part of the tax incentive application process, individuals and entities are screened against databases to check that there are no reports on their involvement in illegal activities such as money laundering and terrorism financing.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The SFO fund is also required to open and maintain an account with an MAS-licensed bank and be subject to the bank’s customer due diligence and ongoing monitoring checks, including detecting any unusual or suspicious transactions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: MAS regularly reviews and refines its regulatory regime.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: It consulted on proposed changes to the SFO regulatory regime in July 2023.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The returns supplement MAS’ ongoing surveillance efforts to maintain the integrity of our financial system.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: MAS and the financial industry will continue to review our surveillance and detection capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: But we need to adopt a sensible and calibrated approach, and should refrain from a knee-jerk overreaction when cases happen from time to time.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Similar to all major international financial centres, it is not possible to have zero incidents given the complex nature of the financial services industry and the high volume of daily transactions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: In addition, combatting financial crime requires a global effort, as illicit fund flows are often cross-border in nature.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: In the Prince Holdings case, the US seized US$15 billion in Bitcoins and the United Kingdom (UK) froze 19 properties.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: It was announced yesterday that Hong Kong and Taiwan have also recently moved to seize substantial amounts of assets and have made arrests.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: All major financial centres have to remain vigilant and work together to combat financial crimes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: We have to remain open to bona fide family offices and genuine investors, to continue growing our financial services industry and creating good jobs for our people.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: High net worth clients also use other service providers such as legal and tax advisors, fund administrators and accounting firms.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Compared to other financial centres, many industry stakeholders already consider Singapore to have more stringent due diligence standards for high net worth clients.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: If we were to tighten further to the point where the processes become overly cumbersome, it will affect our competitiveness, deter legitimate investors and put many local jobs at risk.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This is not the outcome we want for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: There is a Chinese saying that when we open the windows, some flies may also enter.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The solution is not to shut our windows and block out sunlight and fresh air.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: What matters is that we act swiftly to deal with the flies that enter, while also letting in sunlight and fresh air.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This is the approach we take in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: MAS will continue to take a risk-proportionate approach to maintain our status as a trusted financial centre.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: MAS expects our financial institutions to do the same, so that we collectively maintain high standards while keeping our system efficient and competitive.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Singapore will also continue to work closely with our international counterparts to deter and enforce against bad actors who operate across different jurisdictions.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Or would he agree with me that we should adopt a risk-proportionate approach, set high standards, but also maintain the efficiency and competitiveness of our financial system?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: There is a pattern of Ministers and political officeholders asking very rhetorical zeros, like rhetorical questions, which have no meaning, which are like —

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Tiong, you could just respond to the Minister.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: And I do not think it is the Minister's point of view that you should in fact have a zero-risk approach.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I asked him a question to clarify what is his position.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And I respectfully ask him to withdraw that comment and to apologise.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: I will maintain that, that question is not a meaningful question.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I only wanted to clarify the position so that I can give him a considered response.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Earlier, some of his other colleagues, including Mr Pritam Singh, Leader of the Opposition, said that the WP will be a responsible opposition party.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And I hope Mr Tiong bears that in mind in our future discourse.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think that is the key point that I wanted to clarify.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Having high standards is not at odds with being efficient and competitive.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But at the same time, welcome genuine investors, legitimate family offices who want to set up and tap our financial services industry here, and create jobs for our people.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is the approach that Singapore wants to take.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: With regard to the first supplementary question from Mr Tiong, the reports that have surfaced, I mentioned in my main reply that the banks have also been taking action in monitoring the situation and we do reject some of the applications, and some of them, they withdrew after the banks asked questions.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And there is also a system whereby the financial institutions would file Suspicious Transactions Reports (STRs).

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This was something that the banks, the financial institutions have been doing earlier.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But we need to bear in mind that STRs on their own do not equate to offences being committed.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is just a suspicious transaction that is being highlighted.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For the Police, the Police would have to take a look at these early signals, including the STRs that are filed, and conduct further enquiries on their own, including looking at financial intelligence that they have picked up.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And this is what the Police had done.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They had also worked with their foreign counterparts to gather further information on the case, because, as I mentioned in my main reply, this case involves not just Singapore, but many other jurisdictions.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And after the news broke in October 2025, the Singapore Police Force (SPF) reached out to international counterparts to gather more information on criminality with nexus to Singapore to further these investigations and then took action on 30 October, as I mentioned in my main reply.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Tiong also asked, I think he made a comment that there are many flies in the house.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, if we accept that we do not want to have zero risk, and we accept that when we open the windows to let in sunlight and fresh air, that there will be some flies, I think less than 1% to me, does not mean that there are many, many flies in this house.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And I also mentioned that when we detect those flies, we deal with them firmly.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Not to aim for zero, not to go for zero risk.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But when we detect any cases of wrongdoing, when we detect any flies, we go for them.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: MAS will continue to review our rules and our procedures.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think Mr Tiong is mistaken that we only do the checks at the point of application and not on an ongoing basis.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, I am just trying to understand whether this shortened process means that banks would have less time to do their due diligence?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: And in that sense, there is a possibly increased risk that money laundering indications could slip under the radar, in a sense.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In the announcement that I made earlier this year, I made it clear – and this is in the public domain, on public record – that we want to look at how we can streamline some of the processes so that the waiting time is not too long, but at the same time, I emphasised this, we must maintain high standards.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Because Singapore is not competing on the basis of being the quickest, the one with the lowest standards, the easiest to set up an account.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Our competitive advantage is that we are a trusted financial centre.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And if we want to achieve that, we need to maintain high standards.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, that is why I emphasised that any process change and any streamlining should not compromise our high standards.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Having said that, the process changes that we are looking at are also not at odds with maintaining high standards.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I want to assure Ms Lim that it is not to ask the financial institutions to skip steps or to not look out for certain suspicious reports in their due diligence checks.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think we must maintain high standards in that area.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But it is really to clarify – so, what are we looking for, to avoid a lot of toing and froing, and second guessing?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They are still screened, they are still checked.

They will continue to be required to open and maintain a bank account in Singapore, which means that the account will continue to be subject to the bank's customer due diligence and ongoing monitoring checks.
That was my clarification with Mr Tiong earlier.
It is not just at the point of application.
So, this is something which I hope the WP, if you agree that we should not adopt a zero-risk approach, but a risk-proportional approach, then I think we need to strike that balance.
But at the same time, we do not want to do it in a manner which will compromise high standards and affect our reputation.
That is the balance we want to strike.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I agree with the Minister that we should act swiftly in such cases, but at the same time, I am also concerned that yes, while we did carry out the enforcement actions within weeks of the US press release, it may give the impression that we are only doing so after the US has commenced action.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: And so, I wanted to understand, based on what the Minister has shared and based on the SPF's press release, that from the time we received the STR notification in 2024, what have been the reasons for the delay in terms of the actions taken against this group, and whether it is because of the lack of evidence or what were the rationale behind the one year-plus delay?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is kind of similar to what Mr Tiong asked earlier.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I did explain the process of how we deal with STRs that are filed by the financial institutions.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But please allow me to maybe reiterate some of the key points.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This was before the US made public that they are taking action against Chen Zhi and his associates.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These STRs are part of what the authorities would take into account in assessing whether further investigation will be required and further action will be required.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think Mr Chua is familiar with how this works.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: STRs on their own may not equate to an offence being committed.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is just to highlight that could be what looks like a suspicious transaction.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, it is an early risk signal that will need to be looked into, but on its own, does not constitute an offence has been committed.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, the Police will need to look at that and consider other sources of relevant information, including working closely with their international counterparts.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I mentioned in my main reply that Hong Kong, Taiwan and the UK are also some of the other jurisdictions that have done the same.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I think this is the nature of such operations.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We need to share intelligence and information with our counterparts, and depending on how they structure their complex operations, we then work together to see how we can put a stop to it.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I am not sure I heard the Minister accurately, so I just want to ask for good order.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: When an application is before the SFO, will the office do a first round of anti-money laundering search that is usually required by all financial institutions, law firms or accounting firms, when a client approaches with a new business?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, that is on top of what the banks will check.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I am going to move on to the next question.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But before I do so, I would just like to inform Mr Tiong that I am quite disappointed by the exchange just now.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I note that you have withdrawn your earlier comment, but I would like to remind you and all Members of the House, of Standing Order 50(4).

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I consider what you had said just now to be quite insulting and it is beneath the dignity of this House to use such language.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, I remind all Members again; the Member has withdrawn that comment, which is obviously correct.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I would have expected an apology, but I accept that you just withdrew that comment —

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I did want to remind everyone – front bench, back bench.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We are all here for a purpose; we want to maintain dignity and decorum in this House, and the use of such language about a fellow Member of Parliament is not par for the course.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I accept it and I hope that we can, in future, have such discussions in a civilised and polite manner, a respectful manner.
